result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.lexicographical_topological_sort()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find the lexicographically smallest topological order of a directed acyclic graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.lexicographical_topological_sort()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find the lexicographically smallest topological order of a directed acyclic graph. title: >- [Graph.lexicographical_topological_sort()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Find the lexicographically smallest topological order of a directed acyclic graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the lexicographically smallest topological order of a directed acyclic graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58557-L58636){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.lexicographical_topological_sort(key=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Lexicographical topological sort](/assets/graphs/lexicographical-topological-sort.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Getting dressed as a DAG: shirt before tie, trousers before belt and shoes, socks before shoes. Numbered badges give the order returned, which always takes the alphabetically first item whose prerequisites are done: 1 shirt, 2 socks, 3 tie, 4 trousers, 5 belt, 6 shoes. The card lists the same order." width="100%"} Many orders respect the edges of a DAG. This method returns a canonical one: at every step it takes, among the nodes whose predecessors are all placed, the smallest by `key`. The result is deterministic and readable (tasks in alphabetical order whenever the dependencies allow), which is useful for reproducible build orders, stable course schedules, and comparing orders across runs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [key]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional function `key(node_id)` giving the sort key. If `None` (default), nodes are ordered by label (as strings; ties by node ID). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs in order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or has a cycle. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Kahn's algorithm with a priority queue of available nodes, $O((V + E) \log V)$. Matches NetworkX's `lexicographical_topological_sort` with the same key. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Getting dressed: socks before shoes, trousers before shoes and belt, shirt before tie. Among the items that are free at each step, the alphabetically first goes next: ::: {#6f57b01b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["shirt", "tie", "trousers", "belt", "socks", "shoes"]) g.add_edges( [("socks", "shoes"), ("trousers", "shoes"), ("trousers", "belt"), ("shirt", "tie")] ) [g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in g.lexicographical_topological_sort()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['shirt', 'socks', 'tie', 'trousers', 'belt', 'shoes'] ``` ::: :::
